data.title: Middle East Eye: ‘All banks are owned by Jews’: Remarks attributed to MP shake France’s far right
data.author: MEE staff
data.summary:
‘All banks are owned by Jews’: Remarks attributed to MP shake France’s far right
Submitted by
MEE staff
on
Tue, 09/29/2026 - 16:53
Mediapart attributes messages to National Rally president Jordan Bardella, who denies writing them as Le Pen rallies behind him
French far-right Rassemblement National party president Jordan Bardella poses during a photo session in Paris, on 31 January 2024 (Joel Saget/AFP)
Off
Mediapart plunged the French far right into chaos on Monday after reporting that Jordan Bardella, president of the National Rally (RN) party, had made antisemitic comments in private messages.
Bardella, 31, was fighting for his political career on Tuesday after the investigative outlet obtained exchanges dating from 2013 to 2015.
According to Mediapart, the messages show Bardella promoting conspiracy theories about Jews, banks, the French government, and a supposed “new world order dominated by Israel”.
Bardella was 17 years old when the earliest exchanges reportedly took place and had recently joined the party under far-right leader Marine Le Pen.
Bardella denied making the comments and described the reports as part of a “total war” to derail Le Pen’s 2027 presidential campaign.
Mediapart described him as having an “obsession with the supposed Judeo-Zionist control of the country”.
The outlet said it had authenticated the private exchanges but had not publicly released the messages.
In messages cited by Mediapart, Bardella allegedly wrote that “all banks are owned by Jews” and that “the Jew must dominate other peoples, crush them and rob them; a Zionist is necessarily Jewish, and profoundly Jewish. In France, two clear examples are BHL (Bernard-Henri Levy) or (Jacques) Attali. And that is what they want, a New World Order dominated by Israel, with Jerusalem, of course, as its capital.”

Israeli forces sealed off the permanently staffed checkpoint, with large numbers of vehicles backed up and long queues stretching for considerable distances.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Netanyahu says he filed libel lawsuits over October 7 warning allegations
data.author: Fleur Hargreaves
data.summary:
Netanyahu says he filed libel lawsuits over October 7 warning allegations
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Tuesday that he filed defamation lawsuits against allegations that he had received warnings ahead of the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023.
In a post on X, the prime minister called the claims "false slanders", writing that "it is no coincidence that these lies are being spread now, on the eve of elections, by political rivals and hostile foreign actors" who want to topple his "right-wing government" and "install a left-wing-Arab parties government" which seeks to "establish a Palestinian state".
Earlier this month, Israel’s Haaretz newspaper reported that UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed had warned Netanyahu about a possible attack by Hamas 10 days before the events of 7 October 2023.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Manchester City chief claims 'conspiracy' as UAE-owned club found guilty of financial violations charges
data.author: Fleur Hargreaves
data.summary:
Manchester City chief claims 'conspiracy' as UAE-owned club found guilty of financial violations charges
An independent commission on Tuesday revealed that Manchester City Football Club has been found guilty on all 115 charges related to financial rules violations.
The club engaged in "sham" commercial contracts to artificially inflate revenues and reduce costs by more than $1bn, the findings showed.
"The Club’s financial statements had not been prepared and audited in accordance with applicable legal and regulatory principles," the commission wrote.
It was "reckless" and "acted other than with utmost good faith", it added.
In a video sent to staff and players and obtained by Sky Sports News, City's chief executive, Ferran Soriano, called the investigation a "Premier League conspiracy theory".

data.title: Middle East Eye: Saudi Arabia turns to UAE 'white horse' as it gears up to battle Yemen's Houthis
data.author: Mera Aladam
data.summary:
Saudi Arabia turns to UAE 'white horse' as it gears up to battle Yemen's Houthis
Saudi Arabia appears to be mending fences with the UAE in an effort to push back a Houthi military offensive in Yemen that threatens the kingdom’s Red Sea oil export corridor and has seen drones strike Riyadh.
Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman hosted the UAE’s Vice President, Mansour Bin Zayed, in Riyadh on Tuesday, marking the kingdom's most prominent effort yet to reconcile with the UAE after clashing over Sudan, Yemen, and Somaliland.
“The Houthis are bringing Saudi Arabia and the UAE closer together,” Anna Jacobs, a non-resident fellow at the Arab Gulf States Institute, told Middle East Eye.
The two neighbours have been discussing how to collaborate on Yemen for months, western and Arab officials tell MEE, but the talks have been moving slowly.

data.title: Middle East Eye: IRGC issues open letter urging US voters to 'wrest control back from corrupt politicians'
data.author: Fleur Hargreaves
data.summary:
IRGC issues open letter urging US voters to 'wrest control back from corrupt politicians'
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) released on Tuesday an open letter addressed to US voters, calling on them to "wake up" and "wrest control back from corrupt politicians".
In a lengthy open letter, the IRGC directly appealed to American voters, telling them, "you are the ones who empower, with your votes, the government and allow it to do what it does".
"The United States of America is a great nation. To allow vulgar and immoral individuals to continue steering your politics and policies will only further humiliate and undermine the US," the letter continued, urging the American public to "take back control".
This comes ahead of the US midterm elections at a time when Trump's popularity is at an all-time low.

The UAE called the storming of Al-Aqsa a “provocative escalation and an unacceptable extremist act”.

data.author: Fleur Hargreaves
data.summary:
US Treasury Secretary says economic action against Iran to continue
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Tuesday that the economic measures against Iran will continue, targeting those providing financial support to Iran.
“Under Operation Economic Outcast, Treasury will continue to target and disrupt those who provide material, technological, or financial support that allows the Iranian regime to sustain its terrorist enterprise,” Bessent said.
“Treasury will not tolerate any support to the regime and will continue to identify, expose, and isolate Iran’s enablers,” he added.
Meanwhile, US State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott highlighted on Tuesday a $15m reward offered by the US government for information that disrupts the financial mechanisms of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).
